items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: "Fish Market Blues" with Roy Eldridge, that record.

ctx.x: Yes, I think you were. And we made "Emaline" , another tune like that. And I made some records -- well, I made a lot of albums with Dizzy because he didn't have any set big band, of course. And I made quite a few albums with his band. And in the '40s I got to make a record with Louis Armstrong, who was always my big idol. "Fish Market Blues" with Roy Eldridge, that record. I even made an album with Charlie Parker. They had a big band, all the strings and everything.

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: It featured Jimmy Maxwell. He's a great trumpet player, but I mean, I think I should have done the ballad.

ctx.x: If anybody was going to take a ballad on that thing, it should have been me, right? This is after I made "Rockin' Chair." It featured Jimmy Maxwell. He's a great trumpet player, but I mean, I think I should have done the ballad. But they featured him. And it was just like a... Well, it was just the wrong thing, man, you know. It was just like having a .400 hitter and you keep him on the bench.

And see, they never once had to stop for me to read the music, like what they did for those cats. That's another thing. I remember it took them quite some time to get through with that arrangement, you know. The only time they started with me at first was when they first ...(?)..., and he asked me to take a look at it. And I looked at it and I said, "Is it in one?"
